subject: astronomy
title: Stellar Death: Three Endings
welcome_lead: White dwarf, neutron star or black hole — the final mass decides.
meta_desc: A-Level Astronomy: end states of stars and the role of initial mass.
final_note: Initial mass is the single biggest factor in how a star ends.

concepts.def: Glowing shell ejected by a dying low-mass star.
Earth-sized, electron-degenerate remnant of a low-mass star.
Catastrophic explosion ending a massive star's life.
City-sized remnant supported by neutron degeneracy.
A region whose escape velocity exceeds the speed of light.
About 1.4 solar masses — the maximum mass of a white dwarf.

walkthroughs.body_html: Stars below about 8 solar masses puff off their outer layers as a planetary nebula, leaving behind a hot white dwarf. The dwarf cools forever, never to ignite again.

Stars above about 8 solar masses build heavier elements up to iron, then collapse. The bounce drives a supernova. The remnant is a neutron star or, if the core exceeds about 3 solar masses, a black hole.
The Chandrasekhar limit (1.4 solar masses) caps white dwarfs. The Tolman-Oppenheimer-Volkoff limit (around 2-3 solar masses) caps neutron stars. Above that, gravity wins and a black hole forms.

mcqs.q: What determines whether a star becomes a white dwarf or a neutron star?
options: Its mass - low/medium mass becomes a white dwarf; massive stars produce neutron stars or black holes.
Whether it has planets.
Its colour during its main sequence phase.
Because they are the brightest objects in the universe.

mcqs.q: What defines a star as being on the 'main sequence'?
options: It is the hottest stage.
It is the largest stage of a star's life.
Whether it has planets.
It fuses hydrogen into helium in its core.

mcqs.q: Why are Type Ia supernovae used as 'standard candles'?
options: Because they are the brightest objects in the universe.
Because they happen at regular time intervals.
It is the hottest stage.
They have nearly uniform peak brightness, so their apparent brightness reveals distance.
